recipe.goal: Select red-Herschel sources and cross-match with ALMA archive
recipe.method: Select S250<S350<S500 in H-ATLAS catalogues, cross-match to ALMA archive within 5 arcsec using PyVO
Combine MS per field; make dirty maps, estimate global rms with sigma clipping, then clean with tclean to 3 sigma using natural weighting
key_parameters: natural weighting; 216 x 216 pixels; 0.14-0.25 arcsec pixels

recipe.goal: Detect sources and set threshold from false detection rate
recipe.method: Iterative pixel search above threshold within 16.6 arcsec of map centre, masking 1.5 times the beam around each detection; FDR from detections in sign-flipped maps; adopt 5 sigma
key_parameters: FDR from D_F/D_P with maps multiplied by -1; minimum threshold 3 sigma in the test; adopted 5 sigma

recipe.method: Peak pixel flux (PB corrected) and aperture flux from growth curve with apertures 1.5 to 3 beam sizes, divided by the synthesized beam; calibration error added in quadrature
key_parameters: adopt flux where aperture growth curve becomes constant; sigma_ca = 0.1

recipe.method: Discard ALMA detections within 2 arcsec of a MILLIQUAS or SDSS DR17 source
Simultaneous 2D Gaussian fits in 120x120 arcsec postage stamps, with fixed FWHM from Neptune PSF and fixed positions from ALMA and 250 um sources; free amplitude and background
key_parameters: 250 um neighbours found at 4 sigma outside the 16.6 arcsec ALMA radius

recipe.goal: Classify fields into S, PLUM, M and N
recipe.method: By number and separation of 5 sigma detections within 16.6 arcsec; 3 arcsec separation separates PLUM from M; visual inspection for arcs
key_parameters: visual inspection of whole sample for arc-like or extended structures larger than the synthesized beam found 46 cases

recipe.goal: Derive photometric redshift, L_IR and SFR from SPIRE+ALMA photometry
recipe.method: Fit modified black bodies to deblended SPIRE and ALMA 1.3 mm photometry with MMPz, pick best set via lambda_peak-L_IR relation; SFR from L_IR via Kennicutt relation; for PLUM-Fields total ALMA flux is sum of components
Gas mass from the Scoville et al. 2016 relation using 1.3 mm flux density; dust mass from optically thin Rayleigh-Jeans emission with k(nu)=k0 (nu/nu850)^beta
assumptions: T = 25 K mass-weighted cold gas temperature, beta = 1.8

recipe.goal: Test 1.3 mm flux density as a lensing criterion and derive multiplicity and depletion times
recipe.method: Compare S(1.3mm) with PLUM/S-Field class and archival higher-resolution data; count multiples; tau_dep = M_gas/SFR compared with main-sequence and starburst relations
assumptions: alpha_CO = 1 alternative scaling for gas masses
